text: Three weeks ago the Aethermoor Academy burned. Its masters died in the fire, or so the songs say. [long pause] One apprentice ran into the night with a scroll she had copied by candlelight: a prophecy about the Lich sealed beneath the Academy's older ruins. [long pause] It named her. She has not stopped running since. [long pause] At the edge of the Thornwood, the village of Thornhaven lights its lamps. [long pause] The village elder's house stands to the north-west. Lamps are lit in the window. Someone is waiting up. [long pause] The road east into the Thornwood is open now, and something in the square is waiting for you. [long pause] The trees here are scorched black in long streaks, as if cold fire had raked through them. [long pause] Two bandits step out of the thorn trees, blades already drawn. [long pause] "Another one for the hand," one of them mutters. "Take her alive if you can." [long pause] The Academy's lecture hall lies open to the sky, its dome cracked like an egg. Wisps of loose Aether drift between the pillars. [long pause] A scorched lectern still holds an open book, its pages fused to ash. [long pause] Wrapped in oilcloth behind a fallen shelf: a scroll, sealed in violet wax. Untouched by the fire. [long pause] The thorns give way to soft grass and air that tastes of rain. At the centre of the grove stands a tree older than any kingdom. [long pause] Three of its great roots pulse with violet veins, like poison in a wound. [long pause] The root throbs with violet poison. It needs a soul gem to draw the corruption out. [long pause] The root throbs with a sick violet light. The spirit of this grove may know what it needs. [long pause] You press the soul gem into the bark. The violet veins flare, then drain away like ink in water, and the root glows a clean, living green. [long pause] The chapel of the Solarian Order. Its great sun window is shattered, and violet rot crawls over the pews. [long pause] Korvas falls to his knees. The violet fire burns out of his armour, and underneath it is only an old, tired man. [long pause] The southern path out of the Thornwood is open now. It leads down to the Aethermoor ruins. [long pause] The ruins of old Aethermoor sprawl under a storm that never breaks. Cyan crystals grow from the cracks like frost. [long pause] Below the ruins, the Sanctum waits. [long pause] Two hulks of masonry lurch upright before the open sanctum doors, runes blazing cyan. [long pause] The Sanctum is a vault so vast the braziers cannot find its ceiling. On the dais, something tall unfolds itself from a broken throne. [long pause] The Lich staggers. His crown cracks, and the cyan fire pours out of him like water from a broken jar. [long pause] He is dust before the last word. The scroll is warm in Lyra's hands. [long pause] Dawn comes through a crack in the Sanctum's vault for the first time in two hundred years. [long pause] Lyra carries the scroll back to Thornhaven. In the years that follow, she rebuilds the Academy on open ground, far from any tomb, and its first lesson is the story of Vaelthas. [long pause] Orin rides to the Solarian capital with Korvas's sword, and the Order is remade under its old oath. [long pause] Sera returns to the Conclave. This time, they listen. [long pause] Thane teaches the Academy's darkest class: how to say no to a bargain. It is always full. [long pause] And on the first stone of the new Academy, someone carves a line: remember what it cost. [long pause] On a cliff above the Thornwood, the scroll burns away in Lyra's hand, and the sparks drift up into the morning. [long pause] No one writes the Lich's name again. In a generation, he is a story told to frighten apprentices. In two, not even that. [long pause] Orin hangs up his sword in Thornhaven and becomes the worst fisherman the river has ever known. [long pause] Sera stays. Somebody has to show the village children where the roots trip you. [long pause] Thane's brand fades a little more each year. He stops counting. [long pause] And Lyra, for the first time since the fire, sleeps through the night. [long pause] The chest is empty. [long pause] Darkness. Then firelight, and the smell of stew.

text: A traveller, out of the Thornwood at this hour? Come in from the dark, child. The stars must have sent you; we are in need of someone brave. [long pause] [worried] Borin, our merchant, went down the Thornwood road three days ago and never came back. Bandits have grown bold this season. Bolder than bandits should be. [long pause] The Academy studied the Aether, the raw magic that binds the worlds. Its first headmaster tried to bind it to himself. They sealed what was left of him under the old ruins, south of the forest. Lately the seals feel... thin. [long pause] Bless you. The bandits camp in a clearing east of the forest path, past the burnt trees. Take care of yourself, and bring him home. [long pause] Then rest at the Ember Hearth and go with our thanks. But if you change your mind, Thornhaven could use a friend. [long pause] [worried] Any word of Borin? The bandits' camp is east of the Thornwood path, walled in by thorn trees. [long pause] [worried] Borin lives! But "the Lich's hand", directing bandits? Then the seals are not merely thin. Something below is reaching out. [long pause] Thornhaven owes you more than gold. Listen: the forest itself is sickening. The old spirit of the World Tree lives east of the Thornwood path. If anyone understands this corruption, she does. [long pause] And take a sword arm with you. A knight came into the village tonight; he is in the square asking after the ruins. I think you two want the same thing. [long pause] The World Tree Grove lies east, along the Thornwood path. Sylvara, the old spirit, will know what poisons her roots. Go carefully. [long pause] [worried] The southern path to the Aethermoor ruins is open. I feel it in my bones at night, child: something down there is awake and listening. [long pause] Whatever happens below, Thornhaven will keep a lamp lit for you. Come home.

text: Oh, thank the gods, a proper adventurer! Slimes, miss. Slimes out of the Thornwood, eating my turnips down to the stalks! [long pause] Bring me three of their cores, if you would. The Elder keeps a ledger, and he won't believe it without proof. I can't pay much, but I'll pay. [long pause] Fine. Fine! I'll fight them off with a pitchfork, then. Again. [long pause] Three slime cores, miss. They wobble about the Thornwood like they own it. [long pause] Three cores! You did it! Here, take this, and an old vest of mine. It's kept the rain off me for twenty years. [long pause] Not a slime in sight. My little ones won't go hungry this winter, thanks to you.

text: Need steel? You've come to the right forge. None of that bandit junk here. [long pause] Mind the sparks. [long pause] Wolf pelts. Three of them, for the bellows and for lining armour. The wolves in the Thornwood have gone mean this year. Bring me three and I'll forge you a blade worth carrying. [long pause] Good. Don't get bitten. [long pause] Three pelts. Wolves. Teeth. You know the ones. [long pause] Fine pelts. Here: a steel longsword, folded twelve times. It wants a knight's hand, but it'll sell, if you have no knight. [long pause] Door's behind you.

text: Welcome to the Ember Hearth! A hot meal and a soft bed, thirty gold for the whole party. Shall I make up the rooms? [long pause] Sleep well! Tomorrow's troubles can wait for tomorrow. Your journal is safe with me, too; I've written down where you've been. [long pause] Ah. A bit short tonight, are we? Sell some of those pelts at the forge and come back. The stew will keep. [long pause] Potions, ethers, antidotes. Everything a hero forgets to pack. [long pause] Farmer Holt's at war with the slimes again, and Marta wants wolf pelts. If you're handy with a blade, there's coin in both. [long pause] Folk say the forest east of the path is glowing at night. Pretty, if it weren't so purple. [long pause] The cold wind's coming up from the south now. Nobody's sleeping well. Except you lot, I hope. [long pause] The fire's always lit. [long pause] Easy, easy! A woodcutter carried you all in. You were lucky. I took what you owed from your purse; don't argue, you'd do the same.

text: My rescuers! Borin's Wares is open for business again, and for you, the friendly price. Which is the normal price. But friendlier! [long pause] Feathers, potions, ethers! All genuine. Mostly. [long pause] Those Lich Shards that drift through the forest now? Smash one and you'll sometimes find a soul gem inside. Nasty things. Valuable things! [long pause] Mind the bandits! Ha. You don't need to. [long pause] You found me! Oh, sweet mercy. They took my coin, my goods, my good hat. Not this hat. This is my bad hat. [long pause] Listen. They weren't ordinary bandits. They kept talking about "the Lich's hand", like it was a person. Somebody's paying them to watch the roads. [long pause] For a girl with silver hair, coming from the Academy. Er. That's you, isn't it? [long pause] I'll set up shop in the square the moment I'm home. Come and see me. Rescuers get the friendly price!

text: [sadly] Mortals. You carry the smell of lich-shadow on you. But also light. You are not enemies of the forest. [long pause] [sadly] The corruption seeps up from the ruins and into three of my roots. I cannot cleanse them myself. A soul gem pressed into each root would draw the poison out. [long pause] The Lich Shards that drift through the Thornwood are splinters of his will. Break one and, often enough, a gem of his stolen power falls out. [long pause] The voice of the World Tree, child. My roots drink from every ley line in this land. If I fall, the Thornwood's magic dies with me. [long pause] Bless you. The roots that ache are the ones veined with violet: two beside my trunk, one in the southern glade. [long pause] [sadly] Some of my roots still ache. A soul gem for each; the Shards in the Thornwood carry them. [long pause] I feel it. All three are clean. The poison recedes, and I can breathe again. Take this, with the forest's gratitude. [long pause] One more thing troubles me. A name echoes from the chapel beyond my southern roots: Korvas. An iron-hearted knight in your village carries that name like a wound. Bring him to me. [long pause] Knight. I hear a name in your heart that echoes from the shattered chapel beyond my southern roots: Korvas. He is there, and he is no longer a man. [long pause] I will part my roots. Go with care. What waits there wears your old commander's face, but it does not remember mercy. [long pause] The path south lies open. The chapel waits, and so does he. [long pause] The wood breathes easier because of you. Walk safely, friends of the forest.
